claims: The Artemis II mission concluded on April 10, 2026.
The Orion capsule had a safe splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The four-person crew of the Artemis II mission consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The crew returned after a 10-day lunar flyby.
The Artemis II mission was the first crewed deep-space mission in over 50 years.
The capsule hit the upper atmosphere at approximately 24,000 miles per hour.
The crew was retrieved by U.S. Navy divers.
The crew was taken to the USS John P. Murtha for initial medical evaluations.
The mission confirmed the readiness of the Orion capsule and its life-support systems.
NASA and its partners will analyze data from the trip.
